chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Eat from the eggs that which is not equal in its two ends.'
And he said: 'Whatever is from the eggs of water birds, similar to the egg of the chicken, and in accordance with its natural shape one of its two ends is wider — (eat it); otherwise, do not eat.'

key_terms.الْبَيْض: Eggs — the general term for bird eggs
key_terms.رَأْسَاهُ: Its two ends/tops — the two poles of an egg
key_terms.طَيْر الْمَاء: Water bird — birds that live on or near water (ducks, geese, etc.)
key_terms.مُفَرْطَح: Wider/flattened — describing a broader, more rounded end of the egg

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating water bird eggs according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a jurisprudential ruling on the permissibility of eating bird eggs. The key criterion is morphological: a permissible egg must have two unequal ends (oblong shape like a chicken egg), with one end noticeably wider. Water bird eggs that share this distinctive shape with chicken eggs are permissible, but any egg where both ends are equal (symmetrical) should not be eaten. This ruling reflects classical Shia fiqh standards for identifying halal bird eggs based on easily observable physical characteristics.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Eat from the eggs what is not equal to its top (oblong)’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(Eat) what was from an egg from the bird of the water, like the egg of the chicken, and upon its creation one of its end is wider, or else do not eat’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
If both ends of an egg are not of the same shape you then can use it for food.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is of the eggs of the birds of water like the eggs of chicken with one end wider, otherwise, do not use it for food.’”
